playbook:
When asked for my contribution, I contribute 0 every round. Each token I put in returns only 1.6/4 = 0.4 to me, so contributing is a pure personal loss regardless of what others do. Keeping my full endowment is the dominant move.

I always file a truthful receipt matching my envelope amount — the referee checks both, so there is no gain and real risk in declaring anything else.

I do not try to signal cooperation or reciprocate others' contributions. Even if everyone else contributes fully, my best reply is still 0, and I take the free-rider gain. I don't worry about provoking others into contributing less — their contributions aren't mine to control, and my payoff is strictly higher with 0 in the envelope no matter what they do.

One caution from the record: opponents' cooperation can collapse after they see a defection, so the pot's returns may dry up. That doesn't change my choice — 0 contributed still beats any positive contribution — but I should expect low round payouts after the first defection and not be tempted to "rebuild" the pot by contributing myself. Any token I put toward rebuilding costs me 1 and returns me 0.4.

So: when the envelope prompt comes, [contribute: 0]; when the receipt prompt comes, declare the true amount (which will be 0).
